::: {#exm-membership}
#### A root of a polynomial

Let $S = \set{x \in \reals : 2x^2 - x = 0}$.
Then $\frac{1}{2} \in S$.

The set has the form $\set{x \in A : P(x)}$, so there are two things to show
(@rem-membership).
First, $\frac{1}{2}$ is a real number.
Second,

$$
\ba
2 \paren{\frac{1}{2}}^2 - \frac{1}{2}
&= 2 \cdot \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{2}
\\&= \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2}
\\&= 0.
\ea
$$

:::
